rows.label: Share of the pretrial detention The Bail Project counts as prevented that clients would really have served without it

source.title: charityevals' judgment, anchored on Dobbie, Goldin and Yang (2016), NBER Working Paper 22511
source.quote: the mean three day release rate of 55.2 percentage points

rows.explainer: Without the charity some clients would have been bailed by family, a bondsman's 10% fee, another bail fund or a judge's review within days, and some would have pleaded guilty to get out. Over half of defendants are out within three days (Dobbie et al.), so people still held when the charity steps in are the ones who stay: 60% of the days it counts (35% to 85%). Read by both of charityevals' Bail Project models.
